question_text: A government employee is facing an administrative complaint for alleged dishonesty. The investigating committee schedules a hearing but refuses to allow the employee to present witnesses or cross-examine the complainant. The employee claims that this violates his right to due process. Under Article III of the 1987 Constitution, which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Due process is not required in administrative proceedings because they are not criminal cases.
The employee is entitled to due process, which includes the right to be heard, to present evidence, and to cross-examine witnesses.
The employee only has the right to submit a written explanation, not to a full hearing.
The committee may deny the right to present witnesses if the evidence against the employee is strong.
